correctness.rationale: If two A-side vertices are outside, only their corresponding B-side mates can distinguish them, forcing at least n-1 matching indices represented. At equality the landmark set is a transversal of all but one pair. Explicit edge signatures prove that any represented side has size zero or at least three, and conversely those conditions suffice for mixed resolution. One-sided transversals fail domination, balanced transversals dominate, and a full bipartition class supplies the transition-case upper bound. Exhaustive direct verification through n=9 matches all values and stable basis counts.

value.rationale: The result treats a canonical deleted-matching family and reveals a genuine compatibility threshold between mixed resolution and domination: a one-unit penalty occurs exactly for n=4,5,6 and vanishes once balanced mixed bases become possible. The stable-regime classification and exact count make the theorem structurally useful rather than a routine single-family evaluation.
